winner.title: Hot Ukrainian Borscht Recipe (With Beets, Beef, Pork, and More)

evidence.authenticity: Traditional meat-stock hot borscht with beets, cabbage, celery root, parsnip, potatoes, sweet-sour finish with vinegar, sour cream and dill. Author is not Ukrainian, but it is a test-kitchen treatment of the Ukrainian style. Optional kielbasa and caraway are modest additions.
evidence.precision: 21 of 29 ingredients carry weights; vegetables sized with weights (e.g. 1 medium onion 225g, 2 lb beets about 5 medium); 14 sensory cues in steps (until tender, until shimmering, until starting to brown); vinegar adjusted to taste. No pan size and no temperatures.
evidence.testing: Serious Eats test-kitchen recipe. Separates broth from soup, adds vegetables in order of cooking time, and explains make-ahead and freezing. Rating 4.8 but only 6 ratings.
evidence.photos: 4 step images in schema (browning meat, sauteing aromatics, finished soup stages, serving); 60 images on page.
evidence.efficiency: About 4 hr 55 min total, with a 3 hr simmer for the broth. The two-stage method is long but the broth can be made 3 days ahead. Makes 1 gallon, 12 servings.
evidence.access: Short ribs, pork belly, marrow bones, ham hock and celeriac are all at US grocery or butcher counters. Notes give substitutions for the meats.

winner.why: Beat ATK's version with fuller weights, more process photos and a richer multi-meat broth, though ATK is faster.

runnerUp.title: Hot Ukrainian Borscht

evidence.authenticity: Pork-broth hot borscht with the beet, carrot and tomato paste fry-up (zazharka-style) added at the end, dill and lemon. Authentic structure, simplified vegetable list.
evidence.precision: Only 2 of 16 ingredients have weights, but produce is sized (8 oz beets, 1 lb potatoes), 12-inch skillet is named, and 10 sensory cues appear in steps.
evidence.testing: ATK test kitchen, 164 ratings at 4.2. Reasoning text is behind the login, so it was not marked down.
evidence.photos: No step images visible through the schema; step photos may be hidden by the login.
evidence.efficiency: 3 hr 45 min with a 2 hr pork simmer. Vegetables are cooked in parallel with the broth, which is efficient.
evidence.access: Everything is at a standard US grocery.

runnerUp.why: Faster and well tested, but less precise on weights and no visible process photos.

candidates.source: TASTE (Mari Uyehara, adapted from Anya von Bremzen)

notes: Alyona's Cooking is by a Ukrainian author with good step photos but uses Vegeta and garlic salt and gives few weights. The TASTE recipe is adapted from a Russian cookbook and has no structured data, so it was read through WebFetch. NYT has several borscht recipes in the sites output (Winter Borscht, Beets-With-Greens), but these were not read. I did not run a separate sites search for the native-language name.

winner.name: Hot Ukrainian Borscht Recipe (With Beets, Beef, Pork, and More)
